_doc: Engines measured in R1 (docs/reassessment/ROADMAP.md R1.4, track N1). Built by scripts/engines/build_engine.py, in CI (.github/workflows/engines-sm89.yml, compile only, no GPU) and on the server. ${ARCH}, ${NVCC}, ${CUDA_ROOT}, ${DEP_GGML} are substituted by the script. "kind": "torch-extension" (ExLlamaV3) builds a Python wheel with its CUDA extension instead of CMake; its "python" block pins torch and the CUDA it was built with, which the extension's ABI depends on. "r1_template" says why an engine has no scripts/r1 config yet. Pins are full commit SHAs; move a pin only in its own commit with the reason.

llama.cpp.why: master 2026-10-09; contains d6cf9acb2 (--moe-cache-mib) and c811cb8f0 (multi-GPU expert cache); code read for research/R2 at this commit

ik_llama.cpp.why: main 2026-10-09; glm5-next alias (research/R2 §3.5), -muge / -ncmoe expert offload measured on the 3090 host

strata.why: upstream HEAD read 2026-10-08 for the reassessment (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next engine, candidate #1, BRINGUP-qwen38fn.md); flags as its setup.py / Dockerfile build the engine

exllamav3.why: master 2026-10-07, v1.6.0 (docs/reassessment/research/R2-engines.md:71,96): engine of experiment B5 (TP over 4 GPUs without P2P, 'native' backend: R2-engines.md:121); model classes glm5_next, mimo_v2, deepseek_v4, qwen4_exp with MTP (R2-engines.md:141)

python._note: torch 2.14.1 on PyPI requires cuda-toolkit 13.0.3 (pypi.org/pypi/torch/2.14.1/json, read 2026-10-10), so nvcc comes from the same pip toolkit (<venv>/lib/python3.*/site-packages/nvidia/cu13/bin/nvcc) or a CUDA 13.0 install; setup.py@151539c compiles exllamav3_ext with torch.utils.cpp_extension for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST (exllamav3/util/arch_list.py); the server is offline, so torch, its CUDA wheels and the built exllamav3 wheel travel with the bundle

exllamav3.r1_template: none yet: B5 serves through TabbyAPI (AGPL-3.0, R2-engines.md:72) and needs an EXL3 quant >= 4.0 bpw made from safetensors (EXPERIMENTS.md B5); both are UNKNOWN until the weights choice (ADR-005/ADR-009)
